newsitem.title: UK: Higher world coffee output seen not hurting prices.
newsitem.headline: Higher world coffee output seen not hurting prices.

text.p: World coffee output could rise in the 1996-97 crop year after a weather-hit 1995-96 harvest, German crop forecaster FO Licht said in a report on Tuesday.
However with global demand outpacing production, growers' expectations for stable or even higher coffee prices this season "do not seem to be far-fetched," Licht said.
In its first crop estimate for the season, Licht put total crop at 96.45 million 60-kg bags, up by nearly nine million from the weather-affected 1995/96's yield of 87.64 million.
Output from top grower Brazil is forecast at 26 million bags, up by more than 10 million from a year earlier.
In 1994, two severe frosts and a drought devastated some of Brazil's crop and drove London prices to near ten-year highs of $4,140 a tonne.
But prices have fallen since and the robusta coffee futures in London are now trading at $1,414 a tonne.
African coffee production is slowly reversing a long downward trend, Licht said.

"Overnight miralces will not happen but a slight increase may be looked for in 1996/97," it said. Asia's major exporters Indonesia and Vietnam are expected to show significant output increases due to favourable weather.
